source.title: What makes your model a low-empathy or warmth person: Exploring the Origins of Personality in LLMs
source.authors: Shu Yang; Shenzhe Zhu; Ruoxuan Bao; Liang Liu; Yu Cheng; Lijie Hu; Mengdi Li; Di Wang

record.file_problem: The supplied text is a full paper, though some table and figure content is flattened.
record.tranche_reason: The study extracts and checks SAE features in LLMs, including whether selected features can be isolated at different layers and SAE sizes. This bears on the LLM feature-recovery versions, but it does not test the original toy-network superposition setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports personality, social-bias, and safety changes after deliberately steering extracted features. Those induced behavior results do not establish that the behaviors occur without steering, and they do not measure the superposition geometry in the claim. The recorded rows concern the paper's own SAE feature extraction and feature-isolation checks. Other feature-steering results are not cataloged as evidence for the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study uses released GemmaScope SAEs as a tool to pick features for steering personality. Its SAE-related results are steps in its own feature-selection pipeline, not tests of superposition or of SAE features as the model's units. Table 3 is used to choose the steering layer, and the specificity check is a filter applied to the features. Neither reports how features are represented apart from the authors' search. The steering outcomes (TRAIT, SafetyBench, logit differences) are induced-behaviour results unrelated to the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that SAE features (for long-term background factors) and representation directions (for short-term pressures) can steer the personality traits measured by TRAIT without retraining. They report that the 9B model is more stable than the 2B model, and that boosting background features lowers SafetyBench scores, especially for offensiveness. They assert, rather than test, that their filtering makes the selected SAE features monosemantic.
record.recipe_differences: The original source studies toy networks and superposition geometry; this paper extracts selected LLM features with SAEs or activation-difference directions and steers model activations. It does not reproduce the original method.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature isolation depended on SAE layer and size: the authors report better identification with deeper layers and larger SAE size.

fits_no_version.finding: For two ideology concepts in Gemma-2-9B-Instruct, named SAE latents could not be located in 16k SAEs at layers 9 and 20. They were located at layer 31, and in 131k SAEs at all three layers. This is qualitative and comes from a layer-selection search.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether a concept-specific SAE latent can be found depends on SAE width and layer.

record.problems: The feature-specificity check is reported without counts or detailed per-feature outcomes. The layer/size comparison concerns only Liberalism and Conservatism in Gemma-2-9B-Instruct; the table is flattened in the supplied text. Experiments are limited to two Gemma instruction models and released GemmaScope SAEs. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the recorded feature-isolation results.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable; no additional rows on the claim versions were extracted. Personality, social-bias, and SafetyBench outcomes after deliberate steering were left out because they are induced behavior outcomes, not measurements of spontaneous superposition or feature geometry.

untested.parts: All; no toy models, sparsity sweeps or geometry.
All; no neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity analysis.
Not tested beyond using pre-trained SAEs. There is no measure of feature spread across neurons and no independent evaluation of SAE recovery.
Completeness, stability and canonicity are not measured. The layer/size dependence in Table 3 is an anecdotal selection step without metrics.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T2 and its labels are not supported. The only SAE evidence consists of the authors' own selection and filtering steps, reported qualitatively, which makes them circular as tests. The paper's use of the word 'superposed' is informal and does not measure superposition. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, overcomplete sparse features, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometric arrangements.
Neuron polysemanticity, capacity competition, and dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Alternative causes of polysemantic neurons and whether polysemanticity indicates superposition.

Whether features are distributed across many neurons; the study extracts selected SAE features but does not measure broad feature distribution across neurons or compare SAE recovery with other methods.
Completeness, stability across runs or contexts, and whether SAE features are canonical units of the model.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Compared whether Liberalism and Conservatism features could be isolated across SAE layers and sizes.
rows.measure: Whether the selected social-ideology features were identified as distinct or reported as superposed
rows.value: Table 3 reports superposed features at layers 9 and 20 and identified features at layer 31; the table's flattened layout does not support assigning every listed feature name and index to a particular concept and layer with confidence.
rows.note: The authors say deeper layers and larger SAE sizes were more conducive to finding monosemantic, interpretable features. The table is flattened in the supplied text, so individual concept-to-cell assignments are not made.
rows.check: Selection value. Table 3 is a layer/size search used to choose the steering layer (layer 31). It shows whether the authors could find named Liberalism/Conservatism latents, not a measure of superposition. 'Superposed' only means the named feature could not be found. No counts, no criteria and no baseline are given. Readable cells: RES-16k layers 9 and 20 are 'Superposed'; layer 31 gives Liberalism(10223) and Conservatism(12173).

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Compared whether Liberalism and Conservatism features could be isolated across SAE layers and sizes.
rows.measure: Whether the selected social-ideology features were identified as distinct or reported as superposed
rows.value: Table 3 lists Liberalism and Conservatism feature identifiers at layers 9, 20, and 31.
rows.note: The table lists separate identifiers for both concepts at each layer for RES-131k. It does not test whether these features are complete, stable, or canonical.
rows.check: Selection value from the same layer-choice search. Named latents were found at every layer with RES-131k. This says nothing about completeness, stability or canonicity, and not about distribution across neurons.

rows.subject: Gemma-2B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Extracted background-factor features with an SAE and checked their activity against descriptions of other factors.
rows.measure: Specificity of extracted features across descriptions of different factors
rows.value: The paper states that the extracted features remained inactive for descriptions of other factors.
rows.note: The paper describes this as a specificity check, but does not give counts, per-feature results, or a stability test.
rows.check: Circular. Inactivity on other factors' descriptions was the selection criterion, so passing it is guaranteed by construction. The text does not separate results by model, and no counts are given. This should not be a separate per-model row.
